cards.explanation: The answer is like-minded and united in spirit. Paul, the man writing this letter, asks them to be "…like-minded, having the same love, being united in spirit and purpose." That's a whole team pulling the same direction. Picture cookie boxes stacked on a shelf, all lined up facing the same way instead of each one sliding off in its own direction. That's the kind of unity he's after.

The answer is joy. Paul writes, "…then make my joy complete by being like-minded…" He says their unity would make his joy complete. A full cookie jar feels good, friends, but Paul says what fills his is the believers living in unity.

The answer is selfish ambition and empty pride. Paul says, "Do nothing out of selfish ambition or empty pride…" Those are two things to leave out of the mix, friends. Selfish ambition is chasing the spotlight, and empty pride is puffing up with nothing inside. It's like a cookie that rises big in the oven and then drops flat when the door opens, all show and nothing underneath.

The answer is important. Paul writes, "…but in humility consider others more important than yourselves." Humility means the other person gets the spot at the front of the line in your mind. The other person gets the first cookie off the tray, and you wait for the second pan.

The answer is False. Paul writes, "Each of you should look not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others." Notice the words "not only," friends. Your own interests stay on the list, and other people's get added right next to them, like a second pan going in the oven beside yours.

The answer is that He emptied Himself and took a servant's form. Paul says Christ Jesus "…emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in human likeness." The One existing in the form of God took the servant's place. Paul says to let this mind be in us, friends. That's the whole pattern for the believers in Philippi.

The answer is cross. Paul writes that Christ Jesus humbled Himself and became obedient to death, even death on a cross. That's as low as the road goes. The Son who existed in the form of God went all the way down to a cross. Paul wants the believers in Philippi to see how far humility can reach.

The answer is that God exalts Him to the highest place. Paul writes, "Therefore God exalted Him to the highest place and gave Him the name above all names…" He humbled Himself all the way down, and God lifted Him all the way up. That little word "Therefore" is the hinge, friends. The humbling came first, and the lifting follows from it.

The answer is True. Paul says it's "…that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth…" That covers every place there is. Nobody and nowhere gets left out of the lineup. It's a big picture, and Paul painted it wide.

The answer is that Jesus Christ is Lord. Paul says, "…and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father." Knees bow and tongues confess, friends. The whole thing ends up giving glory to the Father. And it started with a Son who went low.

The answer is work out their salvation. Paul writes, "…continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling." He says "continue," because they've always obeyed. And right after, in verse 13, he says it is God who works in them. So they're not doing it alone, friends.

The answer is True. Paul writes, "For it is God who works in you to will and to act on behalf of His good purpose." God works in them in the wanting and in the doing. So the believers in Philippi don't have to supply the whole effort themselves. Honestly, I'd take that deal on any Monday.

The answer is complaining or arguing. Paul says, "Do everything without complaining or arguing…" Everything means everything, bakers. Even the batch that burns and the line that moves slow. It's a short sentence, but it covers a lot of ground.

The answer is lights. Paul says they are to be "…blameless and pure, children of God without fault in a crooked and perverse generation, in which you shine as lights in the world" Lights show up best where it's dark. A little bulb in a dark bakery gets noticed quick. That's what he pictures for the believers.

The answer is that he did not run or labor in vain. Paul says it's "…in order that I may boast on the day of Christ that I did not run or labor in vain." As they hold forth the word of life, his running and laboring will not have been for nothing. He says he'll boast about it on the day of Christ. That's a happy bit of boasting, friends.

The answers are glad and rejoices. Paul writes, "But even if I am being poured out like a drink offering on the sacrifice and service of your faith, I am glad and rejoice with all of you." He says it even if he is poured out like a drink offering. That's a lot of gladness from a man in a hard spot, and he shares it with all of them, together. Joy tastes better shared, like a cookie broken in half.
The answer is False. Paul writes, "So you too should be glad and rejoice with me." He doesn't ask for grief, friends. He invites them to share his gladness and rejoicing instead.
